sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: An adjective placed after the noun, as the predicate, agrees with it in number (szék nagy → székek nagyok), but the same adjective in its usual position before the noun never changes. Quantity words like sok ('many') and néhány ('a few') are always followed by a singular noun.

items.spanish: A nagy asztalok és a kicsi székek.
items.english: The big tables and the small chairs.

sections.content: Notice nagy and kicsi don't change at all in a nagy asztalok és a kicsi székek, even though both nouns are plural — Hungarian only pluralizes the noun, never an adjective sitting in front of it. That's very different from Spanish or French, where the adjective would also need a plural ending.
